definitions.gloss: to exorcise, to purify, to cleanse of evil spirits
definitions.explanation: To perform a ritual purification to drive away evil spirits, impurities, or bad luck. Primarily associated with Shinto practices and traditional Japanese beliefs.

examples.japanese: {悪霊|あくりょう}を{祓|はら}う。
{神主|かんぬし}が{穢|けが}れを{祓|はら}う{儀式|ぎしき}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The Shinto priest performed a purification ritual to cleanse the impurity.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}に{神社|じんじゃ}で{厄|やく}を{祓|はら}ってもらい、{一年|いちねん}の{無事|ぶじ}を{祈|いの}った。
examples.english: At the new year, I had bad luck exorcised at the shrine and prayed for a safe year.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
Godan verb ({五段動詞|ごだんどうし}), う-ending.
- Negative: {祓|はら}わない
- Polite: {祓|はら}います
- Te-form: {祓|はら}って
- Past: {祓|はら}った

USAGE:
Distinct from the homophone {払|はら}う (to pay; to sweep away). {祓|はら}う is specifically religious/ritual purification. The related noun {祓|はら}い or お{祓|はら}い refers to the purification ceremony itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悪霊|あくりょう}を{祓|はら}う: to exorcise evil spirits
- {穢|けが}れを{祓|はら}う: to cleanse impurity
- {厄|やく}を{祓|はら}う: to ward off bad luck
- お{祓|はら}いを{受|う}ける: to receive a purification ceremony
